problem: The text says q at a point depends on "the direct stress on the section". Bending shear flow depends on how fast the direct stress changes along the beam (the gradient), not on the direct stress itself. Where the bending moment is largest, the direct stress is largest but the shear force and shear flow are zero. A student reading this will wrongly size the shear flow from the bending stress value.
fix: For a vertical shear force S (N), q at a point depends on S (that is, on the rate at which the bending moment changes along the beam) and on the distance s along the wall measured from a free edge.

problem: "The point where this line cuts the section is the shear centre" is loose. The line of action of the resultant lies in the plane of the cross-section, so it cuts the section along a line, not at a point. The shear centre is one particular point on that line.
fix: For a vertical shear S, the resultant is a vertical force of magnitude S whose line of action passes through the shear centre. For a singly symmetric section, the shear centre is where this line of action meets the axis of symmetry.

problem: "The sign is opposite the flanges" is too terse to follow. It is not clear whether it refers to the sign of e, of the torque, or of the moment.
fix: Measure e from the web centre line towards the side away from the flanges; a positive e in that direction means the shear centre lies outside the web, on the side opposite the flanges.

problem: The forward references to 5.2, 5.3 and 5.6 are plain text, so a student on a phone cannot jump to the worked distribution or the closed-cell method.
fix: Make them chapter links, for example 5.2, 5.3 and 5.6.
